who: Hannah was the wife of Elkanah, in the hill country of Ephraim. For years she had no children, and his other wife taunted her. At the house of the LORD in Shiloh she prayed in silence for a son, and vowed to give him back. The son was Samuel. She kept her vow, and sang a song of praise.

tidbits.text: The Talmud draws its rules for the central Jewish prayer from her: mean it in your heart, form the words with your lips, and keep your voice down.

The Talmud hears a prophecy in one word of her song: “my horn is exalted in the LORD.” Her son anointed David from a horn of oil, and David's line kept the throne. He anointed Saul from a flask, and Saul's did not.
Every Jewish New Year, synagogues read her story. The Talmud sets it for the first day of Rosh Hashanah, beside the birth of Sarah's son. By tradition, God remembered both women on that day.

facts.label: In the Bible
facts.text: Only in **1 Samuel** 1 and 2. No other book of the Bible names her.

facts.label: Home
facts.text: **Ramathaim-zophim**, or **Ramah**, in the hill country of **Ephraim**. Each year the family went up to **Shiloh**, where Eli was priest at the house of the LORD.

facts.label: Family
facts.text: Her husband **Elkanah**, and his second wife **Peninnah**, who had sons and daughters. Hannah's first child was **Samuel**. Three sons and two daughters followed.

facts.label: Her vow
facts.text: That **no razor** would touch her son's head. It is the mark of a **Nazirite**, set apart to the LORD, in the law of Numbers 6. Samson's mother was told the same of her son.

facts.label: Her name
facts.text: Hebrew for **grace**. Greek and Latin Bibles call her **Anna**.

facts.label: Also called
facts.text: The **Prophetess Hannah**, in the Orthodox Church.

facts.label: Died
facts.text: The Bible does not say. It last speaks of her five younger children.

facts.label: In art
facts.text: Dutch painters of the 1600s, several of them **Rembrandt's** pupils, painted her often: at prayer, as at the top of this page, or bringing the young Samuel to Eli.

portrait.alt: A painting by Gerbrand van den Eeckhout, a detail: Hannah kneels in an orange and green gown and holds the hand of little Samuel, a toddler in a white robe. Her husband Elkanah, in a turban, stands behind them, one hand on a table covered in dark cloth. A metal flask sits on the floor beside her.

west.text: **Hannah**, remembered by Lutherans of the **Missouri Synod**. The Roman calendar has no day for her. It keeps her son **Samuel** on 20 August.

east.text: The **Holy Prophetess Hannah**, mother of the Prophet Samuel, for the **OCA** and the other Orthodox churches.

feasts.note: On 9 December the Orthodox also keep the conception of the Virgin Mary by Saint Anna: two women with the same name, on one day. Churches on the old calendar keep the day 13 days later.

said.lede: The Fathers, in their own words. They took her as a model of prayer, and heard prophecy in her song.

quotes.q: She spoke with hidden prayer, but with manifest faith. She spoke not with her voice, but with her heart, because she knew that thus God hears; and she effectually obtained what she sought, because she asked it with belief.
quotes.who: Cyprian of Carthage, teaching his people to pray. He calls her “a type of the Church”.

quotes.q: Her tears alone uttered a cry more clear than any trumpet. And because of this, God also opened her womb, and made the hard rock a fruitful field.
quotes.who: John Chrysostom, on tears shed in secret, for God alone

quotes.q: Who amongst you would not rather that his son should become a Samuel than that he should be king of the whole world ten thousand times over?
quotes.who: John Chrysostom, urging parents to follow her example

quotes.q: Anna even before Samuel was born promised him to God, and after his birth consecrated him at once, and brought him up in the priestly habit, not fearing anything in human nature, but trusting in God.
quotes.who: Gregory of Nazianzus, telling mothers not to put off their babies' baptism

cite.text: Gregory of Nazianzus, Oration 40, *On Holy Baptism*, chapter 17

quotes.q: When as yet no one was king over that people, whence, if she did not prophesy, did she say what she puts at the end, He gives strength to our kings, and shall exalt the horn of His Christ?
quotes.who: Augustine, in *The City of God*. Israel had no king yet when she sang.

cite.text: Augustine, *The City of God*, book 17, chapter 4

moments.title: Her rival taunted her
moments.text: Elkanah had two wives. “Peninnah had children, but Hannah had none.” Every year he took the family up to Shiloh to worship and sacrifice to the LORD. He gave Hannah a double portion, “for he loved her even though the LORD had closed her womb.” But her rival taunted her, year after year, until she wept and would not eat. “Hannah, why are you crying?” Elkanah asked. “Am I not better to you than ten sons?”

moments.title: A vow at the doorpost
moments.text: After the family had eaten, Hannah stood up. Eli the priest was sitting by the doorpost of the temple of the LORD. “In her bitter distress, Hannah prayed to the LORD and wept with many tears.” She made a vow. If the LORD gave her a son, she would give him to the LORD all the days of his life, and no razor would ever touch his head. Her vow is below, in her words.

moments.title: “How long will you be drunk?”
moments.text: Eli watched her mouth. She was praying in her heart, “and though her lips were moving, her voice could not be heard.” So Eli thought she was drunk. “How long will you be drunk?” he said. “Put away your wine!” She told him she had drunk nothing. She had been pouring out her soul before the LORD. “Go in peace,” Eli replied, “and may the God of Israel grant the petition you have asked of Him.” She went on her way and ate, “and her face was no longer downcast.”

moments.title: A son named Samuel
moments.text: The family went home to Ramah, “and the LORD remembered her.” Hannah gave birth to a son. She named him Samuel, “Because I have asked for him from the LORD.” When the next yearly sacrifice came, she stayed at home. She would bring the boy once he was weaned, she told her husband, to stay at the house of the LORD for good. “Do what you think is best,” Elkanah replied.

moments.title: “I prayed for this boy”
moments.text: Hannah took the boy up to Shiloh with a three-year-old bull, an ephah of flour and a skin of wine. “Though the boy was still young, she brought him to the house of the LORD at Shiloh.” After the sacrifice they brought him to Eli. She reminded the old priest that she was the woman he had seen praying there. “I prayed for this boy,” she said, and she gave him to the LORD for as long as he lived. Then she prayed again, a song of praise: it is below. Elkanah went home, and the boy stayed to serve the LORD under Eli.

moments.title: A little robe
moments.text: Samuel grew up at Shiloh, “a boy wearing a linen ephod.” “Each year his mother would make him a little robe and bring it to him” when she came up with her husband for the yearly sacrifice. Eli would bless them: “May the LORD give you children by this woman in place of the one she dedicated to the LORD.” And the LORD did. Hannah had three sons and two daughters, while “the boy Samuel grew up in the presence of the LORD.” Here the Bible's story of Hannah ends.

words.note: Her words, as 1 Samuel records them. Outside the quiz's own section, every Bible line on this page is from the Berean Standard Bible.

feature.kicker: To Eli, who thought she was drunk
feature.q: I am a woman troubled in spirit. I have not had any wine or strong drink, but I have poured out my soul before the LORD.
feature.ctx: She had been praying in silence, her lips moving. Eli had told her, “Put away your wine!”

quotes.q: O LORD of Hosts, if only You will look upon the affliction of Your maidservant and remember me, not forgetting Your maidservant but giving her a son, then I will dedicate him to the LORD all the days of his life, and no razor shall ever touch his head.
quotes.who: Her vow at Shiloh, in tears.

quotes.q: Do not take your servant for a wicked woman, for all this time I have been praying out of the depth of my anguish and grief.
After the boy is weaned, I will take him to appear before the LORD and to stay there permanently.
quotes.who: To Elkanah, staying home from the yearly journey.

quotes.q: Please, my lord, as surely as you live, my lord, I am the woman who stood here beside you praying to the LORD. I prayed for this boy, and since the LORD has granted me what I asked of Him, I now dedicate the boy to the LORD. For as long as he lives, he is dedicated to the LORD.
quotes.who: To Eli, bringing him the boy.

quotes.q: My heart rejoices in the LORD; my horn is exalted in the LORD. My mouth speaks boldly against my enemies, for I rejoice in Your salvation. There is no one holy like the LORD. Indeed, there is no one besides You! And there is no Rock like our God.

extras.title: Her song, and Mary's
extras.lede: Centuries later, a young woman of Nazareth sang a song much like Hannah's. The *Catholic Encyclopedia* calls Mary's song “very similar in thought and phrase to the Canticle of Anna”. The Lutheran calendar says Hannah's song foreshadows Mary's. Here are some of their lines side by side.

items.title: Joy in God
items.text: Hannah sang, “My heart rejoices in the LORD.” Mary sang:
items.quote: My spirit rejoices in God my Savior!

items.title: The mighty brought low
items.text: Hannah sang, “The bows of the mighty are broken, but the feeble are equipped with strength.” Mary sang:
items.quote: He has brought down rulers from their thrones, but has exalted the humble.

items.title: The hungry fed
items.text: Hannah sang, “The well-fed hire themselves out for food, but the starving hunger no more.” Mary sang:
items.quote: He has filled the hungry with good things, but has sent the rich away empty.

items.title: The lowly lifted up
items.text: Hannah sang, “He raises the poor from the dust and lifts the needy from the ash heap.” Mary sang:
items.quote: He has looked with favor on the humble state of His servant.

myths.claim: Hannah was Saint Anne, the mother of the Virgin Mary.
myths.truth: They are two women with one name: Hannah in Hebrew, Anna in Greek and Latin, Anne in English. Hannah was Samuel's mother, long before. The Bible never names Mary's mother: the name comes from the *Protoevangelium of James*, a book from about AD 150. In it, a childless wife weeps, prays and is given a child. The *Catholic Encyclopedia* calls that story “apparently a reproduction of the biblical account of the conception of Samuel”.

circle.name: Elkanah
circle.text: Her husband, an Ephraimite. He loved her, gave her a double portion at the yearly feast, and let her keep the boy at home until he was weaned.

circle.name: Peninnah
circle.text: Elkanah's other wife, who had sons and daughters. Year after year she taunted Hannah until she wept.

circle.name: Eli
circle.text: The old priest at Shiloh. He took her silent prayer for drunkenness, then sent her away with a blessing. She left Samuel in his care.

circle.name: Samuel
circle.text: Her first child, the son she asked for. He grew up at Shiloh, became a prophet and judged Israel, and anointed its first two kings, Saul and David.

saint.big: Yes, in the Orthodox Church, which honours her as a prophetess on 9 December. Lutherans in the Missouri Synod remember her on 2 September.

churches.note: Rome keeps her son Samuel, 20 August
Her song is a Church of England canticle

paras: The Orthodox call her a prophetess for her song. Their hymn for her day says she saw far-off things as if they were near. The Talmud counts her among Israel's seven prophetesses, for the same song.
The Missouri Synod remembers her for keeping the vow she made before her son was born.
